prompts.positions: Use case: scientific-educational. Premium realistic botanical instructional painting for Japanese vocational agriculture study. One healthy upright tomato plant in soil, isolated against warm ivory background, full plant visible with generous margins, high botanical fidelity and recognizable compound serrated tomato leaves, green textured stems, leaf petioles, young axillary shoot and small tomato fruit truss. This is an observation illustration of plant positions, NOT an instruction to cut every part shown. Clear prominent growing shoot tip at top; a young lateral shoot clearly growing from the axil between the main stem and a compound-leaf petiole in upper-middle; several fully developed compound leaves elsewhere, distinguishable from shoots; a modest cluster of small green unripe tomatoes lower down. A wooden stake alongside, with a soft loose support tie around stake and main stem. Show only ONE main plant, no separate floating parts, no human hands, no tools, no wound or cut lines, no removed leaves, no arrows, no text, no labels, no numbers, no watermark. Make the young axillary shoot distinguishable with several tiny expanding leaves, visibly originating above the leaf petiole in the axil. Light and composition must make the top growing tip, leaf axil bud/young shoot and ordinary mature leaves easy to identify. Rich painterly realism, not flat icons, no primitive circles or geometric diagram. No prescribed remaining leaf or fruit count, no claimed cultivar-specific pruning plan, no brand.
prompts.pollination: Use case: scientific-educational. Original premium realistic botanical instructional painting for vocational agriculture, landscape close-up. Show hand pollination of a squash-family crop: a large open yellow female squash flower attached to a living green vine with a small clearly visible immature ovary swelling immediately behind the flower, and a hand holding a detached male flower by its short green stalk. Male flower petals gently folded backward so its pollen-bearing yellow anther is visible and touches the female flower's central lobed stigma. Clearly distinguish pollen donor anther from the recipient central stigma. Accurate botanical flower anatomy, natural texture of yellow petals and soft pollen, plausible healthy green stems and squash leaf in background; clean warm ivory negative space, gentle realistic shadows, high quality educational painterly realism. Tight but complete framing with both flowers and contacting parts fully visible, some vine and ovary visible, hand fingers anatomically natural, no tools or gloves. No text, no labels, no arrows, no numbers, no watermark, no charts, no primitive circles. Show one illustrative moment only, not a universal pollination protocol or guaranteed fruit set. Independent original composition, not copied source layout. Avoid stamens originating from leaves, avoid pollen on petals instead of stigma, avoid eggplant/tomato flowers. Intended objective: pollen placed on stigma, not on stem or leaf.
